_comment: Machines run_linters.py --remote may use (surveyed read-only 2026-11-02, provisioned for every lint step 2026-11-03). Capabilities are PROBED at run time (lint_remote.probe); the fields here say how to reach a machine, how hard it may be pushed and why a machine is not a lint runner. Nothing here is a secret: keys are named by path and never read.

devbox.note: This development machine (32 cores, 125 GB): the PRIMARY lint runner (Bruce, 2026-11-08), with the full toolchain (rustup 1.98.1 with rustfmt and clippy, cargo-deny, the pytest stack). `lint_slots` heavy lint runs go at once (tools/lint_lock.py), each in its own Cargo target directory and TMPDIR at nice 10; the other machines take a whole run only as overflow when every slot is busy or the load is above the limit. All other machines are optional.

mac1-vm.note: Debian 13 arm64 Lima VM hams-test-debian on the Mac mini mac1 (Bruce's machine; the VM also runs the production FCC ULS sync): lowest priority, 3 workers, never started by the lint runner (a stopped VM is reported unreachable). Provisioned for lint 2026-11-02 and completed for every lint step 2026-11-03 (the dev box's Python test stack, python3-typeshed; its Odoo, PostgreSQL 18 and kopia were already there). Never touched by the provisioning: the fcc-uls-sync unit, the fccsync account and /opt/fcc-uls-sync. Its PostgreSQL has a createdb role for the ai user (tools tests); hams_shared node_modules are installed in the mirror by the runner (npm ci).

bruce17.note: HP Notebook board 81FF (Core i7-7500U, 2 cores / 4 threads, 7.6 GiB, 256 GB SATA SSD), Debian 13 x86-64, wifi only (RTL8188EE; hp-notebook-81ff-support fixes its PCIe error flood). A light helper and clean-room test host: lint fan-out, one Odoo module test at a time, small CI. Provisioned 2026-11-04 with tools/provision_build_host.sh via lint_remote.py provision bruce17 --apply.

bruce16.note: Optional OVERFLOW machine (the reserve policy: `apply_reserve` in lint_remote.py), used only when the primary runner is saturated and never for the browser: it is somebody's interactive workstation, so it has the lowest priority (nice 19), at most half its cores, no step that needs a browser (Chrome), a low load limit, and it is skipped while a login session is open. Provisioned and verified 2026-11-08 with tools/provision_build_host.sh (Debian 13 x86-64, 16 cores, 15 GB); reached as ai@bruce16.lan with the ssh default identity (no key path is named here).

bruce-yoga.note: Debian 13 x86-64 build and test server (8 cores, 15 GiB, GitHub Actions runner bruce-yoga-linux). Stays awake on AC (logind drop-in); on battery it may suspend, which shows as unreachable. Provisioned for every lint step 2026-11-03 (tools/provision_build_host.sh via lint_remote.py provision bruce-yoga --apply): the dev box's Python test stack, Odoo 19.0.20261029 (service disabled), PostgreSQL 18 (local; createdb role for the ai user), kopia, Go 1.24, Chrome.

mac1.reason: macOS host and Bruce's own machine; its Linux VM mac1-vm is the lint runner. System python is 3.9 (the linters need 3.10+), no cargo or node.

bruce-yoga-win.reason: Windows build VM behind bruce-yoga (PowerShell, no POSIX tar/sh pipeline); used for Windows relay builds only.

Bruce_Thinkpad.reason: Windows laptop (PowerShell); used for Windows relay builds and the Windows side of certificate login.

hams1.reason: PRODUCTION. Never a lint, test or build host.

cache_budgets._comment: Disk budgets of the persistent lint caches (tools/lint_cache.py, docs/runbooks/LINT_CACHES.md). cargo_gb: cap of EACH warm Cargo target directory (one per repository and toolchain); free_floor_gb: free space the filesystem must keep (the cache prunes, then clears itself, rather than fail a run); results_mb: cap of the per-file result caches. `hostnames` lets a runner find its own entry. Environment overrides: HAMS_LINT_CARGO_GB, HAMS_LINT_FREE_FLOOR_GB, HAMS_LINT_RESULTS_MB.
